scope: Test-internal durable local resume in a fresh OS worker after a lost Docker-create acknowledgement. Public CLI update, resume and reviewed-plan verification remain unproven by this probe.

distributions.python_source_tree_digest_format: SHA-256 of compact sorted JSON mapping package-relative .py paths to file SHA-256 values, without a trailing newline.
distributions.tested_archives_note: These identify the tested archives; later documentation and evidence changes can change archive hashes.

contract.reviewed_plan_checksum: Synthetic per-run test marker, not a genuine public reviewed-plan checksum.
contract.worker_one_exit: Controlled process exit after durable interruption record and normal lock release; not SIGKILL.
contract.worker_two: Fresh OS process, independently loads protected state/control and reacquires the real local lock.
contract.worker_two_provider_mutations: One exact candidate start; no create, TERM, remove, volume mutation or offset reset.

limitations: This invokes internal backend, observer and executor APIs; it does not expose or verify public CLI update/resume, a genuine reviewed plan, or a modified on-disk SQL project.

Worker one deliberately records recovery_required and exits cleanly. The fresh-worker restart and lock reacquisition are real, but abrupt death, SIGKILL and lock loss during a write are not injected here.

The failed response is injected after one successful real Docker create. Other crash prefixes and archive/control write failures are covered separately by unit tests, not by this real-provider fixture.
Only the local filesystem state backend is exercised by this Docker/Kafka probe; PostgreSQL resume has separate verification.

One local Docker broker, one partition and PLAINTEXT do not establish authenticated deployments, distributed fencing, throughput, retention-loss recovery or comprehensive lifecycle exactly-once guarantees.
The reused runner selects exactly_once_v2; the observed record and offset results are bounded evidence, not a general production-safety claim.

The full close contract is evaluated by the real observer before journaling. This probe records the raw exit code and checkpoint offset vector, but does not duplicate the standalone observer probe's raw close status and Docker timestamp surface.

Fixture containers, data volumes and networks were removed after exact ownership checks. Their demo data is not recoverable; raw evidence and worker records remain in the recorded temporary directories.
